overview: Two of the three routes that converge on C3 activation in the complement system, differing mainly in what triggers them.
genZNote: Classical waits for an antibody invite. Alternative just crashes the party on any microbial surface.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A complement activation pathway triggered by antigen-antibody complexes binding C1q.
aspects.valueB: A complement activation pathway triggered spontaneously by low-level C3 hydrolysis on microbial (or other unprotected) surfaces, without antibody.

aspects.label: Trigger
aspects.valueA: Requires antibody (IgM or IgG) bound to antigen.
aspects.valueB: Antibody-independent — activated directly by pathogen surfaces lacking complement regulatory proteins.

aspects.label: Initiating Components
aspects.valueA: C1q, C1r, C1s complex binding to the Fc region of bound antibody.
aspects.valueB: Spontaneous C3 hydrolysis ("tickover"), factor B, and factor D.

aspects.label: Part of Immunity
aspects.valueA: Bridges adaptive immunity (antibody-dependent) to the complement system.
aspects.valueB: Purely innate — does not require prior antibody formation.

aspects.label: Convergence Point
aspects.valueA: Converges on C3 convertase formation (C4b2a), leading to the shared terminal pathway.
aspects.valueB: Converges on a distinct C3 convertase (C3bBb), leading to the same shared terminal pathway (membrane attack complex).

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: Antibody-independent, spontaneous activation on pathogen surfaces.
